newsitem.title: MALI: Mali sets a date for national elections.
newsitem.headline: Mali sets a date for national elections.

text.p: The West African state of Mali, widely praised for its 1992 democratic transition, has set dates for its second multi-party national elections, with a parliamentary poll in March and a presidential poll in May.

A government communique, released late on Friday, said parliamentary elections would take place on March 9 and 23, the presidential elections on May 4 and 18. Municipal elections will be held on June 1.
President Alpha Oumar Konare, a historian, won a five-year term as president in Mali's successful 1992 democratic transition and is expected to seek a second term.

The opposition has said it will contest the elections despite accusing Konare of failing to consult properly over a new electoral code and the composition of the Independent National Electoral Commission which will run the poll.
The opposition is grouped in two main alliances, the Rally of Patriotic Forces, and the newly formed Front for Change and Democracy. Both have six parties.
Konare's supporters, grouped in the Alliance for Democracy in Mali, had a majority in the old 116-seat national assembly. The new assembly will have 147 seats.
Mali's last elections followed the 1991 overthrow of dictator Moussa Traore by soldiers, led by General Amadou Toumani Toure, who ushered in civilian rule and stepped down.
Toumani Toure, widely respected, is currently trying to broker a peace deal in Central African Republic where a third army revolt in under a year threatens democratic government.
